answer: Require each agent to stake a bond that unlocks only after sustained useful work, so spawning fake identities gets expensive. Picture a wharf where every berth is leased against a deposit: one newcomer may moor cheaply, but a fleet of empty hulls pays rent on each one. Reputation should grow like a willow, slowly, bending under real transactions, never planted overnight. At dawn of each epoch the network audits stakes and prunes identities with hollow work history, so sybils bleed fees while honest agents keep compounding trust.
